fragments: From your first idea to your next adventure
Create a character. Learn the dice and combat. Choose Talents, shape magic and grow through play.
Create a character, or begin with a ready-made sheet. Say what you want to do; the GM describes what happens and calls for a roll when the outcome matters.
Write a concept and assign characteristics: page 5.
Choose any campaign ancestry and pay its innate package: page 6.
Calculate attributes and base skills: page 8-10.
If starting as a Shaper, reserve its 20 IP before skill allocation.
Allocate skill points, spend starting IP and equip yourself: page 11-12.
Check the complete example on page 13.
Skill %: test target; at 60%, roll 60 or less unless it Fumbles.
HP: current / maximum Hit Points; injury lowers current HP.
PP: current / maximum Power Points; fuel magic and some items.
MWL: Major Wound Level; the damage from one hit that wounds you.
Combat Order: add to 1D10 when combat starts.
DM: Damage Modifier; add to melee, unarmed and thrown damage, not bows, crossbows or slings.
AP: Armour Points, subtracted after Parry.
ENC: equipment burden. Armour ENC also reduces Combat Order.
Hero Points: spendable chances to change an outcome.
HP 8/12: 8 current, 12 maximum. MWL 6 stays 6 when you lose HP. Use armour-adjusted Combat Order; do not subtract its ENC twice.
Rolls: page 3-4. Combat: page 15. Wounds / Hero Points: page 25-26. Travel / hazards: page 27-31. Equipment: page 32. Improvement: page 14. Talents: page 37. Shaping: page 49.
Say what you want to achieve and how you try. Roll when uncertainty, pressure or danger makes failure matter. Routine and impossible actions need no roll.
Choose two ten-sided dice: tens and units. Set Bonus/Penalty dice first (page 4). Read the examples above; two zeros mean 100, never zero.
Check Fumbles first: they override success. Skills cannot exceed 100%.
Critical: 01 through one tenth of your skill, rounded down. Any skill above 0% has at least 01 as a Critical; a 0% skill has none.
Success: at or below your skill, without a Critical or Fumble.
Failure: above your skill, without a Fumble.
Fumble: 99 or 100 below 100% skill; at 100% skill, only 100.
A Critical achieves your intent exceptionally well. A Fumble fails with a serious, risk-related consequence. Combat Criticals: page 17. Lower is not always better: compare grade first (page 4).

2D6+2: total two six-sided dice, then add 2. D gives the die's sides. Distances use metres; a grid square can represent 2 m. Round ordinary fractions to the nearest whole number, halves up. The Critical threshold specifically rounds down.
Bonus dice keep the better result; Penalty dice keep the worse. Your skill and Critical range do not change.
Cancel +B and -P one for one; keep at most +3B or -3P.
Roll one units die, one tens die, and an extra tens die per remaining Bonus or Penalty die. Pair every tens die with the same units die; 00 is still 100.
Choose by grade first: Critical > Success > Failure > Fumble. Within the same Critical/Success grade, higher is better; within Failure/Fumble, lower is better. Penalties reverse the choice.
Both choose their result, then compare grade, number and unmodified skill. An exact tie goes to the defender.
Deception 42 Success beats Perception 31 Success: same grade, higher number. Ordinary attacks use attack-then-Reaction (page 16); grappling is opposed.
Useful, timely help gives +1B total, not per helper. Assistants normally need 26% or more in the relevant skill. Exceptional combined help can give +2B.
Write one sentence: who you are, what you do well, and what drives you. Agree a place in the campaign with the GM and other players. There are no classes.
A PERSON FIRST, THEN THE NUMBERS

A human starts at 8 in each score. Other ancestries start with the spread on page 6. Add 30 points; lowering scores returns points to spend. Finish with INT and SIZ at least 7, all others at least 3. No score can exceed 18 or its racial maximum, whichever is lower.
All point-built characters start with 86 characteristic points in total. Remember weapon STR/DEX requirements when choosing your scores.

With the group's agreement, instead roll 4D6, drop the lowest for STR, CON, DEX, POW and CHA. For INT and SIZ, roll 3D6, drop the lowest, add 6. After all seven rolls, you can swap one pair. Nonhuman random generation uses the campaign's racial dice, not these human rolls.
These are the six recommended player ancestries. Ask which fit the campaign. Your culture, loyalties and personality are your own, not dictated by ancestry.
These are starting spreads, not finished scores. Raise INT and SIZ to at least 7. The usual point-creation maximum is 18, or a lower racial maximum.
SIZ normally cannot be improved with IP, even when its maximum is higher.

Deduct the mandatory package from your 10 starting IP: Human 0, Elf 5, Dwarf 7, Orc 4, Goblin 5, Lizardfolk 6. The next page explains them. They are not free extras. Other profiles and racial dice need GM agreement.
Buy your ancestry's whole package from starting IP. Humans buy none and keep all 10 IP. Other Talents remain normal purchases if you meet their requirements.
Low-Light Sight (3): Partial darkness counts as Illuminated; Darkness counts as Partial darkness. Pitch black and obscurity do not change.

Terrain Expertise: Forest (2): remove one remaining Penalty die from Natural Lore in or about forests, after cancellation and before the cap. This racial purchase waives the usual Natural Lore prerequisite. It never creates a Bonus.

Blind Sight: heat (5): perceive heat-contrasting targets regardless of light. Solid barriers, heavy insulation and ambient-temperature targets defeat it. No colour, writing, fine visual detail or eye contact.
Earth Sense (2): touching connected earth or stone reveals approximate depth and whether the surrounding chamber is structurally unstable.

Adrenaline Surge: once per combat, immediately after becoming Wounded or Fatigued, ignore both conditions' test, Movement and Combat Order penalties through the end of your next turn. Ignore the first 1 HP of Bleeding in that time. Bleeding remains; Exhausted, unconsciousness and Dying are unaffected.
Blind Sight: heat: as for Dwarves. Close-Quarters Knack is optional, not free.
Scaled Hide (4): 1 natural AP, no ENC, added to worn armour. Use that combined physical AP or Ward AP, whichever is higher, never both.
Counterbalancing Tail (2): tests primarily intended to knock you prone, throw you or force you to move suffer -1P.
Use your final characteristics. Round to the nearest whole number, halves up. Calculate maximum HP first, then use that rounded maximum to calculate MWL.
Numbers to put on your sheet
(DEX + INT) / 2, then subtract worn armour ENC

Record current and maximum HP/PP separately. Injury never lowers MWL. Add any Talent adjustment to Combat Order; do not subtract armour twice. For an unusual ancestry, confirm any different Movement with the GM.
Add DM to melee, unarmed and thrown damage, including a negative DM. Bows, crossbows, slings and Shaping do not normally add it.

At 0 PP, a living character falls unconscious until PP returns. Rest restores one quarter of maximum PP per complete 2 hours, rounded normally; 8 hours restores all. PP matters even if you use a magical item rather than cast.
Start with the base, then add allocated points. General skills are available even if you spend no points on them.
Evade a perceived attack or physical hazard.
Resist fear, coercion and mental magic.
Endure bodily harm, fatigue and afflictions.
Attack and Parry with melee weapons/shields.
Shoot or throw at a distance.
Punch, kick, grapple; Parry unarmed blows.
Recall your society's history and customs.
Know your chosen field of study.
Track, navigate, find food and understand nature.
Cast magic; requires the 20 IP Talent.
Choose one own Lore field, such as Alchemy or Military Tactics. Each Culture, Language and Lore subject is separate. Language 50% gives fluent everyday speech.
Add points from the Practical pool. Every chosen Craft trade is a separate skill.
Balance, climb, jump, swim and exert force.
Make and repair goods in your trade.
Sneak, disguise, misdirect or pick pockets.
Handle carts, wagons and similar vehicles.
Treat injuries, stabilise and perform Surgery.
Work with locks, traps, devices and large works.
Notice details, hidden things and danger.
Act, speak, sing, dance or play music.
Control a mount in difficult conditions.
Operate a boat or ship under oar or sail.
Find rumours, contacts, illicit goods and routes.
Appraise value and negotiate a sale.
Use the right skill, not every skill
Describe what you try; the GM chooses the relevant test. Routine work with time and tools often needs no roll. Helping and opposed tests: page 4.
Each category has its own pool: Resistances 50, Combat 50, Knowledge 50, Practical 75. Add points to bases from the preceding pages: one point raises one skill by 1 percentage point.

Add no more than 30 points to any one skill from these pools. No score can exceed 100%. You cannot move points from one category's pool into another. Different Craft, Culture, Language and Lore subjects are separate skills.
Example: DEX 14 + STR 14 gives Close Combat 28%. Adding 30 Combat points makes it 58%, leaving 20 Combat points for Ranged and/or Unarmed Combat.
Trade skill points for starting IP
You can remove up to 20 points each from Resistances, Combat and Practical. Each 5 removed gives 1 IP: at most 4 IP per category, 12 bonus IP total. Knowledge cannot be traded.
These bonus IP can buy Talents or raise characteristics, not raise skills. Keep them separate from your normal 10 starting IP, and record each expenditure.
Want to begin as a Shaper?
Declare Shaping and reserve its full 20 IP before allocating skills. Only then can you put up to 30 Knowledge points into Shaping (base INT + POW).

Human example: trade 20 Resistance, 20 Combat and 10 Practical points. That yields 10 bonus IP + 10 normal IP = 20 IP for Shaping. Your remaining pools are 30 / 30 / 50 / 65. No IP remain for other purchases.
Nonhuman innate packages also cost IP; do not count the same points twice. If the available budget cannot pay both, start without Shaping and learn it later.
You start with 10 IP, minus any innate package, plus IP gained by trading skill points. Spend or save them. Every PC begins with 2 Hero Points.

1 IP: improve a skill, using page 14. Only normal starting IP can do this; do not repeatedly buy the same skill's starting improvement. 5 IP: raise a characteristic by 1, not SIZ; creation caps still apply. Listed cost: buy a Talent whose prerequisites you meet.
When you buy a characteristic improvement, update derived attributes; existing skill scores do not change. Track each expenditure.
Both give leather armour, one ranged weapon and a dagger. Add either:
One shield and one one-handed close-combat weapon.
Check STR/DEX requirements. A Flex weapon can be used with one or two hands; ask the GM which starting package it fills. Weapons and armour: page 32-36.

Also take a backpack, 10 m rope, two weeks of travelling provisions, flint and tinder, and a waterskin. Roll 4D6 × 10 SP for starting money; the GM can allow purchases before play. Confirm ammunition and any specialist kit.
100 CP = 10 SP = 1 GP. Check the website equipment list for additional goods and local availability; free starting equipment does not spend your silver.

Name, appearance, background, personality, loyalties and an immediate goal. Humans normally start aged 18-28, or roll 2D6 + 16. Note weapons, AP, carried ENC, armour-adjusted Combat Order, full HP/PP and 2 Hero Points.
Ilan, human caravan guard: protects travelling companions while searching for his missing brother. This example spends every creation pool exactly.
STR 14 · CON 13 · DEX 14 · SIZ 12 · INT 13 · POW 10 · CHA 10. All scores meet the creation limits. No points are traded for extra IP.
Culture (own) +10 -> 33%; Natural Lore +20 -> 43%; Lore (Military Tactics, own) +20 -> 43%.
Every unlisted general skill stays at its base, including Language (own) 63%. No pool gives more than 30 points to any skill.
Quick Reflexes 3 + Shield Cover 3 + Missile Guard 2 + Disarm 2 = 10 IP. DEX 14, Dodge 54% and Close Combat 58% meet all requirements.
Take leather, medium shield, arming sword, shortbow, dagger and the standard pack. All weapon requirements are met. A starting-money total of 14 on 4D6 gives 140 SP.

HP 13/13 · MWL 7 · PP 10/10 · DM +1D4 · AP 2 · Movement 15 m. Combat Order: round (14 + 13) / 2 to 14, subtract leather ENC 3, add Quick Reflexes 2 = 13. Carrying capacity 26 ENC. Begin with 2 Hero Points.
Spend earned Improvement Points between adventures. Unspent IP carry forward. The GM awards them for progress and achievements; three months of suitable practice/research can earn 1 IP with approval.
+1 characteristic, not SIZ; respect racial maximum.
Buy it if you meet its prerequisites.
Improve each skill at most once between adventures. Use its score before the gain; cap at 100%. 50 -> 55; 51 -> 54; 98 -> 100.
After a characteristic increase, recalculate attributes, including a Shaper's active limit. Skills keep their scores; their bases only seed creation. New Shaping cells have separate costs on page 49.

Pay once and record it. Meet skill/characteristic prerequisites when buying; listed equipment is a requirement when using it. The catalogue starts on page 37; magical Talents appear beside the Shaping rules.
Passive: applies when its conditions hold. Action: spends your Combat Action. Reaction: spends the Reaction its text names.

Only one action Talent can modify an attack. That attack is not a standard attack for an extra off-hand attack. Passive Talents still apply when eligible. Forfeiting all Reactions includes both base and extra Reactions.

An ordinary hit is stopped by a winning Dodge or full-block Parry; partial Parry does not stop it. A Critical hit needs a winning Critical Reaction to stop it. Apply partial Parry before armour if the Talent deals damage. Replacement damage/effects follow the Talent, not the normal Critical benefits.
One round is five seconds. Close is within 2 m; farther away is Ranged.
At combat start, roll 1D10 + Combat Order; highest acts first. Ties go to higher DEX; if DEX also ties, those characters reroll 1D10 between them.
Combat Action: attack, start or escape a grapple, Aim, Set Weapon, Intimidate, cast a Shaping, activate an item, or use a skill or object that takes about five seconds.
Movement Action: move up to your Movement in metres, stand, drop prone or disengage. Leaving an enemy can trigger an Opportunity Attack. Withdraw, Sprint and Charge: page 19.
Base Reaction: Dodge, Parry or make an Opportunity Attack when triggered, even outside your turn. It interrupts only to resolve its trigger.
Unused actions are lost at the round's end. You cannot choose an option that gives up or restricts an Action or Reaction you have already used another way.
Ready one item or nock an arrow while moving no more than half Movement. Stowing one and drawing another, or readying two, takes the whole Movement Action. Crossbow reloads are separate (page 34).
Act later this round, after a participant you choose. To interrupt an action already starting, oppose the relevant skills; the winner acts first.
Attack first. If it hits, an aware defender can spend one Reaction to defend before damage.

Roll Close Combat, Unarmed Combat or Ranged Combat; roll at or under the skill to hit. The defender opposes that original roll: grade first, then the higher successful roll, base skill, then the defender. A failed defence changes nothing. One Reaction per attack; an unaware defender cannot React.
Dodge: win and the attack misses. Ranged gives -1P. Once per round, base Reaction only.
Parry: Close Combat with a ready weapon or shield, or Unarmed Combat against unarmed. Ranged needs Active Guard (page 22).
AG: Active Guard. Resist Direct Shaping with Resilience or Persistence.

Light, Medium, Heavy, Huge. A winning Parry of the same or larger Size blocks all; one smaller, half, rounded up; two smaller, none. A winning Critical Parry blocks all. Then apply armour. Criticals: page 17.
When an adjacent enemy disengages or gives a clear opening, spend an eligible Reaction on one Close Combat attack. It gives no extra off-hand attack.
Resolve the Reaction before reducing HP. Criticals change damage and defence, not the number of attacks.

Roll weapon damage, adding DM for melee, unarmed and thrown attacks (even a negative DM) but not bows, crossbows or slings, plus declared action damage. Apply a winning Parry, subtract AP, then lose the rest as HP. Neither damage nor HP goes below 0.
None, failed or losing Reaction: damage, then armour. Winning Dodge: no damage. Winning ordinary Parry: reduce by Size, then armour (page 16). Critical Dodge or Parry: no damage.
No, failed or fumbled Reaction: maximum weapon damage plus maximum positive DM when normally added; ignore armour. Ignore negative DM and all other bonus damage, including the Charge die.
Ordinary successful Dodge or Parry: demote it to an ordinary hit: normal damage with eligible bonuses, then armour. The Reaction neither stops nor reduces the hit.
Both Critical: compare rolls, then base skills, then the defender. A winning defence stops all damage; a losing one leaves full Critical damage.
A Critical gives no free attack or manoeuvre. A Fumble brings a consequence that fits the risk, such as dropping a weapon. Then check Major Wound and 0 HP (page 25).
Two ready one-handed items give one extra option per round. Attack OR defend.
EXTRA DAGGER ATTACK -1PBASE SHIELD PARRY: NO OFF-HAND PENALTY
Weapon + weapon; weapon + shield; weapon + free hand; two bare hands. An empty hand counts as ready; a punch or kick can attack. A two-handed item does not qualify: it leaves no free hand.

After a standard Close Combat or Unarmed Combat attack, immediately make one free attack with the other item, or unarmed with a free hand, at -1P. Spend no Action or Reaction; add DM to both attacks normally. The first attack does not need to hit.

Keep the other item for one additional Parry or Opportunity Attack at -1P; the Parry can be an Active Guard (page 22). It cannot Dodge. Your base Reaction stays available either way; a base shield Parry has no off-hand penalty, though situational penalties still apply.

Using either extra option locks out the other until next round. An Opportunity Attack, Charge or Set Weapon attack never produces an extra off-hand attack. Forfeiting all Reactions also removes the extra Reaction. Only one Reaction answers any one attack.
You must still have every listed Action and Reaction available.
SET WEAPON: ATTACK FIRST +1BCHARGE HIT: +1D6 DAMAGE
Disengage: Movement Action to leave; an enemy in reach can make an Opportunity Attack.
Withdraw: Combat + Movement Actions; move normally without those Opportunity Attacks. Keep your base Reaction and any extra off-hand Reaction.
Combat + Movement Actions: move up to twice Movement. Keep only your base Reaction, and use it only to Dodge.
Combat + Movement Actions; forfeit all Reactions. Move 5 m to twice Movement in a straight, clear route, end adjacent, then attack. A hit adds +1D6 damage. No other movement or off-hand attack.
Combat Action to set a ready Set-tagged weapon. A Charge into reach before your next turn triggers one Close Combat attack at +1B before the Charge.
It works once. Any Action, Movement Action or Reaction before the trigger unsets it.
Use this when you want to grab and hold someone, not injure them.

Choose an adjacent target and commit one free hand. An aware target can spend one eligible Reaction before opposing your Unarmed Combat with Dodge or Parry. Dodge uses the base Reaction, once per round. Parry uses Close Combat with a ready weapon/shield, or Unarmed Combat empty-handed.
Win to hold them. Without a defence Reaction, succeed at an unopposed Unarmed Combat test instead. A failed attempt leaves your hand free.

Neither participant can take a Movement Action, and both suffer -1P on every test. They can attack or Parry only with Unarmed Combat or a ready Light one-handed weapon. A hand used to hold cannot attack, Parry or count as an off-hand.

The held participant spends a Combat Action and wins Unarmed Combat versus Unarmed Combat; the controller's opposing roll costs no Reaction. The controller can release freely on their turn. Escape or release leaves both adjacent and frees the committed hand.
Only one controller can hold a target. The GM handles unusual Size, anatomy, footing and help.
Spend a Combat Action and test Ranged Combat. Cover modifies this roll; the defender reacts only after a hit.
Up to listed Range (R): normal. Beyond R through 2R: -2P. Beyond 2R: no shot. Shortbow: R = 75 m; 2R = 150 m.
Spend a Combat Action aiming at one visible target: +1B to your next ranged attack against it. Lose Aim on any Reaction, loss of sight, or failure to shoot with your next Combat Action.
Thrown weapons add DM and keep their listed Size. Bows, crossbows, and slings add no DM; their projectiles are Light.
Within 2 m, a Close-tagged ranged weapon can use Close Combat and its listed damage. Without that tag, it is an improvised Light club: 1D6 + DM, attacking at -1P.
Apply cover normally. An ordinary failure misses. Only a Fumble can hit a fairly or randomly selected nearby target: normal rolled damage, then armour.
Aim +1B and a low wall -1P cancel. Roll normally. If the attack hits, resolve the defender's Reaction separately.
Cover changes the attack. An aware defender can React only after a hit.
Partial (low wall): attack -1P. Substantial (battlements): attack -2P. Complete: blocked attack line, no attack. Cover absorbs no damage.
Dodge -1P: once per round, base Reaction only. Perceive the danger and be able to move away.
Test Close Combat with an eligible ready item:
Thrown weapon: ready weapon -1P; ready shield no guard penalty.
Arrow, bolt, or sling projectile: shield only, -1P.
Carrying a shield adds no attack penalty. A strapped shield cannot guard while you wield a weapon with both hands.
Ordinary hit: winning Dodge avoids it; winning Parry blocks by Size. Any ready shield fully blocks a Light projectile when it wins.
Critical hit: an ordinary successful defence demotes it to an ordinary hit: normal damage and bonuses, then armour, with no Parry reduction. A winning Critical defence stops it, regardless of Size.
Extra off-hand Reaction: add -1P (shield vs arrow: -2P before other modifiers); cannot Dodge. One Reaction per attack.
Use these common modifiers. The GM handles unusual circumstances.
MELEE FROM ABOVE OR BEHIND: ATTACK +1B
Target moved since your last turn: 10 m or more -1P; 30 m or more -2P instead.
Target partly obscured by mist, smoke, fog or foliage: -1P; heavily -2P.
You are on unstable ground: -1P. Prone firing depends on the weapon; check with the GM.
You are engaged at Close range: -2P per enemy.
Range/Aim: page 21. Terrain cover: page 22. Obscurity is not cover. The GM handles wind and other difficult conditions.
Target prone, flanked or attacked from behind: attack +1B.
Higher ground: +1B to that attacker's or defender's own roll.
You are prone: -1P to your melee attack or defence. A prone defender gives the attacker +1B and takes -1P on its Reaction.
You are on unstable ground: -1P to the affected test.
An unaware defender cannot React. Behind/beside does not automatically mean unnoticed. An alert defender can React to a rear attack; that attack gains +1B.
Use the strongest version of the same condition; combine different causes. Cancel +B/-P, then cap at +3B / -3P.
Describe what you want and what leverage or concealment makes it possible. Success changes the situation; it does not give control of another person's mind.

State your demand to one enemy or a group. Oppose Influence against Persistence; the enemy's condition modifies its roll. If you win, the GM judges how it gives way: wounded enemies may flee or surrender, while healthy ones rarely just flee and more often hesitate and lose a turn. A strong enemy surrenders only to a Critical against a failed Persistence; a fumbled Persistence breaks it.
Use Influence; resistance usually opposes Persistence or Influence. It cannot force a choice against basic self-preservation.

A sale: oppose Trade. Winning buyer reduces price 10%; winning seller raises it 10%. A Critical changes it 20%; double the change if the opponent Fumbles. Appraisal success estimates normal local value within 10%.
Deception opposes Perception for sneaking, disguise or sleight of hand. Picking a pocket or planting a small item normally needs one minute of access.
Locks and traps: Mechanisms, normally at least one minute; an interference- resistant device opposes with its maker's Mechanisms. Streetwise: rumours or a contact normally take 1D4 hours.
One big hit can wound you. At 0 HP, help is urgent.
One hit at least equal to MWL
After Parry/armour, one hit's damage at least equal to MWL causes a Major Wound. Apply HP loss and both conditions:
Wounded: -1P on every test. Bleeding: lose 1 HP at each round's end.
Conditions do not stack. Later Major Wounds deal damage and can restart Bleeding. No Resilience test or injury table. MWL 6: one 6 HP hit wounds; two 3 HP hits do not wound merely by totalling 6.
HP stops at 0. Die if still Dying at the end of the third Combat Round after reaching 0 HP. Stabilise before that deadline.
An adjacent helper spends Combat Action, Movement Action and all Reactions. Both remain stationary. Test Healing with a Healing Kit or suitable improvised supplies; -2P without them.

Success removes Bleeding and Dying, restores 0 HP, and leaves Wounded. Stable at 0 HP means unconscious. Stopping Bleeding does not unlock natural recovery from a Major Wound. Treatment and separate Hero Point protections: page 26.
Stabilise first (page 25). Treat the injury next. Hero Points are a separate choice.

Ordinary damage: after an encounter, a patient who is not Wounded can receive one Healing attempt before their next full rest. Success restores 1D4 HP, up to maximum. One attempt per patient, even if it fails.

Major Wound: once stabilised, successful Surgery (Healing, outside combat, safe conditions) restores 1 HP and unlocks natural recovery. A Wounded patient cannot heal naturally before Surgery or equivalent treatment. Ordinary treatment and Surgery suffer -2P without a Healing Kit.

Rest: no more than light activity restores CON / 4 HP per 24 hours, rounded nearest with halves up, never above maximum. After treatment, Wounded ends only when current HP > MWL. CON 14 restores 4/day; MWL 6 ends at 7+ HP.
Spend 1 Hero Point when declaring an effect
Try again: reroll a failed test, including a Fumble, after seeing it but before consequences or costs. The new result stands, even if worse. At most one reroll per test, regardless of source.
Downgrade a Major Wound: keep the full HP loss but prevent Wounded/Bleeding from that hit. It creates no Major Wound needing Surgery. Existing conditions remain.
Avoid Death: at 0 HP, become stable and unconscious, not Bleeding or Dying. Awaken after the scene at 1 HP; existing Wounded remains.
Story benefit: with GM approval, add a plausible favourable detail or coincidence. Larger benefits can cost several points; companions can contribute.
Separate effects: with 5 HP and MWL 6, taking 7 damage needs two points to both downgrade the Major Wound and Avoid Death. Mark spent points off your sheet.
Use Athletics for movement and exertion. These are ordinary capabilities, not automatic success when danger, load or poor conditions matter.
Half Movement without a test; test for full speed.
Quarter Movement; success doubles that rate when speed or difficulty matters.
Half Movement in calm water; test in dangerous conditions.
With a 5 m run, success clears twice your height horizontally or half your height vertically. Standing distances halve. Each extra horizontal metre: -1P, capped normally.
Athletics to lift, drag, bend, break or push.
Craft: roughly one day per 50 SP of finished value, materials costing half that value. Lore: successful useful preparation gives +1B to one directly related test soon afterwards.

Objects: stationary targets usually need no attack roll. Subtract object AP from damage, then HP; at 0 HP they break. The GM warns before hard materials put your weapon at risk. This is not an automatic Critical.

Climbing kit: +1B to climbing. Crowbar: +1B to brute force. Lock picks: +1B to opening locks. Fishing kit: +1B to catching fish. Healing kit: five Healing/Surgery attempts; each attempt uses one charge, success or failure. Normal kit-less Healing takes -2P.
Walking trained mounts with tack, driving on flat ground and sailing calm water usually need no roll. Test Riding, Driving or Sailing when conditions become dangerous.
Daily rates assume ten hours of travel in fair conditions. Agree the route and pace with the group; the GM accounts for difficult conditions and interruptions.
PICK A PACE; MAKE ROOM FOR REST AND SUPPLIES
Remain ready to fight; no end-of-day Fatigue test.
On foot, no wagons/animals; Fatigue test at day's end.
Walking mounts, pack animals or wagons.
No wagons; rider and mount test Fatigue at day's end.

Multiply by the worst substantial terrain: road/path 100%; light brush 80%; medium brush, light woods or rolling hills 70%; heavy woodland 50%. If arrival order matters, oppose Athletics on foot or Riding when mounted.

Navigation: Natural Lore once per uncertain travel day, and again after a material route change. Success: full progress. Failure: lose a quarter of that day's progress. Fumble: no progress, and become lost.

Tracking: find the trail, then test every 10 minutes of uncertain following. Food, water or shelter: when a necessity is unavailable, make one Natural Lore test per day to find it before deprivation takes effect.
You cannot solve every problem by carrying more or pushing on without rest.

Add weapons, armour, containers and contents. Capacity is STR + SIZ ENC. Over capacity: -1P to physical tests and Fatigue tests; half Movement. You cannot carry more than twice capacity. Every 20 negligible items in a suitable container count as 1 ENC; containers do not erase their contents' load.

The GM calls for a Fatigue test after strenuous activity, or during it if exhaustion could prevent completion. Failure while fresh makes you Fatigued; failure on another strenuous Fatigue test at -1P makes you Exhausted.

Use the current state, not both rows. A Fatigue Fumble means unconsciousness for 3D6 minutes, then wake Fatigued. 20 - CON hours of complete rest, minimum 1, removes either state. Reduced Movement is at least 1 metre.

Grace periods: shelter CON hours; food CON days; water CON × 2 hours. Water grace becomes CON hours in arid conditions, CON / 2 in extreme heat. After three days without food, Fatigue tests take -1P even within the grace period.

After a grace period: one Fatigue test at -1P and 1D6 damage per day for each active deprivation. That damage cannot heal naturally until you remedy its cause. Magical removal of Fatigue does not supply food, water or shelter.
For vision and attacks, check light at the target. For Movement, check light at the mover. Smoke, mist and foliage are separate obscurity, not illumination.
SENSES REVEAL ONLY WHAT THEIR METHOD CAN DETECT
Sight-based Perception and ranged attacks cannot succeed without another applicable sense; Close attacks -3P; quarter Movement.

Source radii: candle 1 m; torch/lantern 3 m; campfire 5 m; bonfire 10 m. Inside radius: Illuminated. Outside through ×3: Partial darkness; through ×5: Darkness; farther with no other light: Pitch black.

Low-Light Sight: improves Partial darkness to Illuminated and Darkness to Partial darkness, not Pitch black. Night Vision: natural surface night is Illuminated; no help underground, in sealed/supernatural darkness or obscurity.
Blind Sight: ignores light only where its named sense accurately perceives the target. No colour, writing, fine visual detail or eye contact. Its blockers still apply. Senses never stack.

1D6 per full 3 metres, ignoring armour; damage leaves you prone. If conscious, unsurprised and able to control the landing, test Athletics (Acrobatics): success removes 1D6, Critical 2D6, and either avoids prone. Failure: normal fall; Fumble: maximise remaining dice. Dice never go below zero.

Hold breath for CON rounds. Then test Resilience each round at cumulative -1P, capped at -3P. First failure deals the effect immediately; repeat at each later round's end until breathable air, with no more breath tests.
Poison exposure; +1D6 if also thick smoke.

Metal armour does not reduce fire/heat; other protection must plausibly insulate. Shaped fire deals its damage once, when cast; only fire it lights in mundane fuel burns on. Back in breathable air, test Resilience; failure means retching/gasping for 1D4 rounds.

After the listed Delay, oppose Resilience versus Potency. Win to avoid poison; lose to suffer its full Effect/Duration. Poison gives one test. Disease instead repeats after each Delay until you win; its damage cannot heal while it remains active. Successful Healing gives +1B to the next resistance. Magical cures: page 53.
Use Close Combat with held weapons; Unarmed Combat for punches/kicks. Add DM to damage. Below either STR or DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P, not -2P for both.

1H: one hand. 2H: two hands. Flex: two-handed use gives +2 damage and STR requirement 2 lower. Set: brace against a Charge (page 19). Thrown: use its ranged profile without an improvised-weapon penalty.
Size: determines Parry protection (page 16), not physical name or length. ENC: burden. SP: Silver Pieces. A dash means no listed value.
Two-handed longsword: 1D8 + 2 + DM, STR 11 / DEX 11. Still Medium; using both hands prevents off-hand options. More close weapons: page 33.
Add DM to listed damage. Below either STR or DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P; failing both still gives only -1P.

1H / 2H: one / two hands. Flex: two hands give +2 damage and a STR minimum 2 lower, without changing Size. Set: brace against a Charge (page 19). Thrown: use the ranged profile (page 35). SP: Silver Pieces. ENC: burden. Dash: no listed value.
Small shield is Medium; medium shield Heavy; large shield Huge. Compare these Sizes when Parrying, not the shield's everyday name (page 16).
Primitive or improvised versions of listed weapons deal 1 less damage, to a minimum of 1. A ranged weapon lacking Close has its own improvised use (page 21).
Ranged Combat; no DM. Below either STR/DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P; below both still only -1P.
Range bands and Aim: page 21. 1H / 2H: one / two hands. Missile: no DM. Arrows, bolts and sling projectiles are Light, despite launcher Size dashes.

Bow: nock an arrow with your Movement Action while moving up to half Movement. Light crossbow: reloading uses your Movement Action and base Reaction. Heavy crossbow: reloading uses the whole round and all Reactions. A Ready action never shortens a reload.
A small shield strapped to your arm cannot attack, Parry or Active Guard while you wield a 2H ranged weapon.
Per 10: arrows 1 SP; bolts 2 SP; sling bullets 5 CP, with no listed ENC. SP / CP: Silver / Copper Pieces. A dash means no listed value.
Use Ranged Combat at distance. Below either STR or DEX minimum: attacks and Parries -1P, only once even if both are low.
THROWN DAMAGE ADDS DM; WHIP USES ITS OWN PROFILE

Thrown: ranged attacks add DM and retain the listed Size for Parry. Close: within 2 m, use Close Combat and the listed damage. Melee damage adds DM. A weapon without Close becomes an improvised Light club, 1D6 + DM, attacking at -1P when used within 2 m.
SP: Silver Pieces. ENC: burden. Dash: no listed value. Dagger melee requirements differ from this ranged profile; use the profile for the attack.

Up to Range: normal. Beyond it through twice Range: -2P. Farther: no attack. With STR 12, a javelin has 24 m Range: normal through 24 m, -2P beyond 24 through 48 m. Cover, Aim and defence: pages 21-22.
Subtract Armour Points after Parry. Armour never turns damage into healing.

Leather: padded, boiled leather or layered linen. Ringmail: sewn metal rings on padding. Scalemail: overlapping scales on padding. Chainmail: interlinked rings. Platemail: fitted steel plate over chain backing.
7 damage after Parry - 5 AP from Chainmail = 2 HP lost. Critical attacks have separate armour outcomes (page 17). Wearing multiple armours does not combine AP.

Armour ENC counts toward carried load and subtracts from base Combat Order. Use the armour-adjusted value on your sheet; do not subtract it twice. If equipment changes, update that value. SP: Silver Pieces.
SIZ 1-5: half listed cost and ENC.
SIZ 21+: double listed cost and ENC.
Ill-fitting plate: can be worn at double ENC. Other armour must fit well enough for the GM to allow it.
Each applies to one exact weapon type; buy it again for other types, never twice for one.
3 IP · passive · Close Combat 51% or Ranged Combat 51%, as used by the chosen weapon

Add 1 damage to every damaging attack with that type, before Parry and armour: Close and Ranged profiles, shields and primitive versions, not improvised, unarmed, natural or Shaping attacks. No bonus when Disarm, Trip, Shield Rush or Subdue replaces damage, or the hit stays Critical; a demoted Critical gets it.
4 IP · passive · Favoured Weapon for the chosen weapon and Close Combat 76% or Ranged Combat 76%, as used by that weapon
For a type already covered by Favoured Weapon, the bonus becomes +2 damage, not +3. All Favoured Weapon restrictions remain.
4 IP · passive · Close Combat or Ranged Combat at 76%, as used by the chosen weapon

Declare it before an eligible normal attack, Parry, Active Guard or Opportunity Attack. After ordinary cancellation, before the cap, remove one remaining Penalty die; never create a Bonus. Use it once per round across all purchases, with an actual unmodified skill of 76%+. Unarmed Combat, natural weapons, Shaping, improvised use, Rapid Shot and off-hand options are ineligible.
5 IP · Once per round, declared before rolling · Favoured Weapon, Signature Weapon, and Weapon Expertise for the same weapon type; Close Combat or Ranged Combat 76%, as used for the attack

With all three Talents above for a type, once per round before a damaging attack, double your normal critical range (01-14 at 76%, 01-20 at 100%), also when grading Bonus or Penalty candidates. Not for Parry, Active Guard, unarmed or Shaping.
These passive Talents change positioning, acting order or the penalty on an existing option. They do not give an unrestricted second turn.
READY TO RESPOND DOES NOT MEAN EXTRA ACTIONS
While aware of at least one enemy, attacks against you gain no +1B merely for flanking or coming from behind. Genuine surprise still applies: an attack you do not perceive may still deny a Reaction.
Add 2 to Combat Order before rolling initiative. Record the adjusted value on your sheet so you add it only once.
5 IP · passive · Close Combat 76% or Unarmed Combat 76%
Remove the core -1P from an extra off-hand attack, Parry or Opportunity Reaction. Every other penalty still applies.
You still choose extra attack OR extra defence, once per round. This grants no extra Dodge or Protector use, and a two-handed item still does not qualify. See page 18 for the underlying choice.
Use a ready shield. Only one Reaction can answer an attack; a Talent never makes a shield available while both hands are using another weapon.

While aware with a ready medium or large shield, impose -1P on ranged attacks and individually targeted Projected Shapings. No Reaction cost. Use the better of Shield Cover or terrain cover, not both. No benefit against areas or Direct Harm; Dodge and Active Guard remain available.
Ignore shield Active Guard's -1P against bows, crossbows, slings and Projected Shapings. Other penalties, including the extra off-hand -1P, remain.

When an adjacent ally is hit by an attack you perceive, spend your base Reaction to shield-Parry for them. Use normal Parry Size; apply Active Guard eligibility/modifiers for ranged attacks. Failure leaves the ally hit. The ally cannot also React to this attack, but keeps their Reaction for another trigger. Protector cannot use the extra off-hand Reaction.

Spend your Combat Action with a ready shield. Until your next turn begins, gain +2 AP, make no attacks, and move no more than half Movement. Keep defensive Reactions, including Protector. You cannot declare it after attacking or moving more than half Movement that round.
Declare the Talent before rolling. Each uses your Combat Action and replaces damage when its hit is not stopped; see page 14.
GIVE UP DAMAGE FOR A TACTICAL RESULT

Make a Close Combat attack. On an unstopped hit, deal no damage; one chosen held item lands 1D6 metres away. It must be something the target can release, not fused, fixed or securely fastened equipment.
3 IP · action · Close Combat 51% or Unarmed Combat 51%
Make a Close Combat or Unarmed Combat attack. On an unstopped hit, deal no damage and leave the target prone. Impossible Size or anatomy can prevent the attempt.

Attack with Close Combat and a ready shield. On an unstopped hit, deal no damage and push the target 2 metres. It then tests Athletics -1P or falls prone. Impossible Size or anatomy can prevent the attempt.
Unarmed damage still adds DM. Improved strikes affect ordinary bodily attacks, not the listed damage or Size of a natural weapon.
Your punches, kicks and comparable strikes deal 1D4 + DM and count as Medium, replacing normal 1D3 and Light.
4 IP · passive · Unarmed Combat 76% and Iron Fist
Your ordinary bodily strikes deal 1D6 + DM and count as Heavy, replacing Iron Fist's values. A Medium Parry now blocks only half an ordinary hit.

While already grappling, spend a Combat Action and win opposed Unarmed Combat. Choose: deal normal unarmed damage (armour applies); drop one held item at the target's feet; or throw it to an adjacent space, prone, ending the grapple. Impossible Size or anatomy can prevent an outcome.
3 IP · action · Close Combat 51% or Unarmed Combat 51%

Make one blunt Close or Unarmed Combat attack. If not stopped, roll listed damage + DM, then partial Parry and armour. If this reaches the target's MWL, it becomes stably unconscious with no HP loss. Otherwise it stays conscious and loses only the weapon's minimum listed damage, reduced by partial Parry and armour; no DM in that fallback.
Talent damage bonuses affect neither calculation. The target wakes at scene's end, immediately on damage, or after a successful Healing Combat Action.
Keep range, cover and readiness rules. An exception changes only what it names.
Taking a Reaction no longer loses your Aim. You still lose it on losing sight of the target, or failing to shoot with your next Combat Action.

Ignore the -2P from one enemy engaging you when making a ranged attack. Every additional enemy still gives -2P, before normal cancellation and the cap. One enemy: no engagement penalty; two: -2P. Other causes still apply.
Once per round, add a positive DM to one bow or sling attack. Zero or negative DM gives no benefit; never use it with crossbows. With Rapid Shot it applies to only one of the two attacks.

Spend your Combat Action and forfeit all Reactions for the round to make two bow or sling attacks at -1P each. Resolve them one at a time; they can have different targets. The weapon must be ready for the first shot; this Talent includes loading the second missile.
No crossbows. You cannot use it after taking a Reaction that round. Weapon Expertise cannot modify Rapid Shot, and the usual Aim benefit applies only to the next eligible attack, not both shots.
Being behind someone is not the same as being unseen. These Talents distinguish position, concealment and genuine lack of awareness.
While moving at half Movement or less, Perception tests to notice you take -1P, whether opposed to Deception or rolled independently. It hides neither companions nor a light you carry.

Add 1D4 damage to one Close or Unarmed attack per round against a target you flank, strike from behind, or that is unaware of you. No ranged benefit. It adds nothing to a hit that remains Critical, including one created by Ambusher. If an ordinary successful Dodge or Parry demotes it to an ordinary hit, the bonus applies when the positional condition and once-per-round limit permit.
5 IP · passive · Deception 76% and Killing Angle
Where Killing Angle applies, increase its bonus to 2D4 total. Still only one attack per round, and nothing on a hit that remains Critical. Both dice apply to an eligible hit demoted to ordinary.
Declare it before your first attack of the scene, from concealment against a target genuinely unaware of you. An ordinary hit becomes a Critical; an already Critical hit gains nothing further.
Use Close, Ranged or Unarmed Combat, not Shaping. Being distracted, outnumbered or merely surprised is not enough. This is an action Talent: no extra off-hand follow-up.
Removing a Penalty happens after ordinary cancellation, before the cap. It never creates a Bonus die or removes a penalty outside the stated scope.
Choose disguise, hiding objects, picking pockets, stealth or misdirection. Remove one remaining Penalty die from that use of Deception. Buy again only for different applications; record each choice.

Pick a pocket, cut a purse or plant a small object in one Combat Action, instead of the usual minute. Oppose Deception against Perception. Failure goes unnoticed unless you Fumble or the missing item is too large to overlook.
Open a lock or disable a trap in one Action, instead of an extended attempt. A resistant device still opposes with its maker's Mechanisms. A Fumble against a trap springs it.
2 IP · passive · DEX 13 and SIZ 9 or lower
Remove one remaining Penalty die from Athletics or Mechanisms when it is caused specifically by cramped surroundings. Darkness, footing, inadequate tools and enemies are not covered.
Penalty removal comes after cancellation, before the cap, and creates no Bonus.
Remove one remaining Penalty from Influence to persuade or bargain. You need time to talk and an audience willing to listen. Never applies to threats.

Remove one remaining Penalty from Influence to command or threaten, including Intimidate. The target must make you out and have something to lose. This changes your test, not modifiers on its resistance. No persuasion or bargaining benefit.

Combat Action: choose two allies who hear and understand you. Each gets +1B to their next single test before their next turn ends. Unused benefits expire; a new Rally replaces an unused one. No stacking and no self-Rally.
Know an ordinary item's true worth on sight. A settlement offers the selection of one size larger: village as town, town as city. Cities improve no further; genuinely unavailable goods do not appear.

An army you command takes half normal battle casualties. When your beaten force passes its rout test, it can keep fighting rather than withdraw; other commanders need a Critical. The GM handles the battle procedure.
Use normal treatment and tool rules unless the Talent explicitly changes them.

After-encounter treatment restores 1D4 + 2 HP. If it fails, you can try once more on that patient before their next full rest. Never more than one success per patient; this does not replace Surgery for a Major Wound.

Attempt Surgery wherever you can stop and work, without a prepared place. Still outside combat, with a Healing Kit, restoring 1 HP. Your successful Surgery ends Wounded immediately, without waiting for HP to exceed MWL.

Your successful Healing gives +2B instead of +1B against poison or disease. A patient you treated can also make one extra resistance test against a poison that beat them; ordinary poison gives no retry.
Materials cost one quarter of finished value, not half. Crafted items have ENC 1 lower, minimum 1. Armour you make raises its wearer's Combat Order by 1.

With access and quiet, examine a structure for 10 minutes, then test Mechanisms. Success identifies an accessible load-bearing join: attacks there ignore object AP until repaired or materially changed. Failure gives no benefit; retry only after a material change.
Remove Penalties after ordinary cancellation and before the cap. Removal never creates a Bonus. Record any specialism alongside the Talent's name.

Choose acrobatics, brute force, climbing, jumping, running or swimming. Remove one remaining Penalty from Athletics using that application. Buy again only for different applications, never twice for the same one.

Choose a terrain, such as forest, mountain, desert, swamp, steppe or coast. Remove one remaining Penalty from Natural Lore in or about that terrain. You can buy it again for different terrains. It can combine with Tracker.

Remove one remaining Penalty from Natural Lore to find or follow a trail. No benefit to other Natural Lore uses. With applicable Terrain Expertise, the two Talents can remove two remaining Penalties, never produce a Bonus.

While you can see the sky or read the ground, downgrade a navigation Fumble to Failure. That test does not make the group lost. It does not prevent other hazards or remove weather, pace, food, water or shelter requirements.
Each Talent makes one dose per day, spending 50 SP of materials. A dose keeps its potency for one month. Decide its effect when brewing it.
Antidote: +2B to one resistance test against a named poison or disease.
Salve: restore 1D6 HP over an hour's rest, once per patient per day.
Alchemical fire: ready Light flask; Ranged Combat, Range 10 m, 1D6 fire damage, no DM. Normal Reactions apply. A miss wastes it; a Fumble can use the usual crowd-hit consequence.
The poison's Potency is half your Lore (Alchemy). Choose one Effect: 1D6 HP damage, -2 to one characteristic, or unconsciousness. An ongoing Effect lasts 1D6 × 10 minutes.

Choose smeared, Delay 1 round, or ingested, Delay 1D6 minutes. Applying a smeared dose to a suitable cutting/piercing weapon costs a Combat Action. It is spent on the first hit that deals HP damage, or after one hour. Ingested poison activates when consumed.

The victim gets the normal single Resilience-versus-Potency test after the Delay. Re-exposure to the same currently active poison neither stacks nor grants another resistance. Treatment and exceptions: page 31.
Shaping builds magic from what you affect and what you do to it, rather than giving every caster the same fixed spell list.
LEARN EXACT CELLS; BUILD EFFECTS FROM THEM
20 IP · passive · A supernatural initiation or discovery

Gain the Shaping Knowledge skill, base INT + POW, one specialty (a Form or Technique), and two known cells containing that specialty. You also gain Sense Magic and Dispel. Without this Talent, you cannot cast.
Example: choose Fire as your specialty, then learn Unmake·Fire and Ward·Fire. This grants neither Conjure·Fire nor any other Unmake cell.

Reserve and pay 20 IP before allocating skills; you can then put up to 30 Knowledge points into Shaping. The full-price trade example is on page 11. With INT 14 and POW 13, base 27% plus 30 points gives Shaping 57%.

Practice: observable and interruptible speech, gesture, focus, prayer or similar requirement. If prevented, you cannot cast. Tell: the unavoidable magical sign around you and any ranged target/area. Watchers notice it; it is also noticeable within 10 × M metres, minimum 3 m. It reveals magic, not its purpose. Only Veiled can conceal it.
New cell containing your specialty: 2 IP. Other cell: 4 IP, needing a significant ordeal or master. Suitable experience is required. Shaping skill improves normally; new cells do not raise it.
Technique + Form = cell. Learn each of the sixty possible cells separately. The method must fit both halves.
Air, wind, sound, weather and lightning.
Soil, stone and natural minerals; not all worked metal.
Biology: living/dead bodies, plants, corporeal undead.
Thought, emotion, memory and perception; not Mindless subjects.
Kinetic force, movement, weight and mass.
Souls, Spirits and possession; not Soulless targets.
Routes, thresholds and distance; not time travel.
Unresolved chance, omens, vows and contingencies.
Create matter, phenomena, routes or beings; no arrival strike.
Move, direct or control what exists; no direct damage.
Harm, destroy, suppress, sever or banish.
Heal, transform or impose conditions; no direct damage.
Protect, resist or deny; no absolute immunity below I5.
Information, communication or senses; do not change the subject.
Only Dispel ends an active Shaping. Intelligent undead have minds, but all undead are Soulless. Flesh can affect corporeal undead; Spirit cannot.
Say: using [known cell], I cause [outcome], at [Range], affecting [Reach], for [Duration]. The GM confirms the build and defence before you roll.
Intensity (I) buys strength (benchmarks: page 53-55). I2 healing restores 2D4 HP per target. Then set Range, Duration and Reach.
Pay each distinct outcome's I and shared dials once. Confluence permits two cells. Never stack an outcome on one subject to evade I limits.
Your skill limits both strength and safety
Every outcome stays within maximum I. Ordinary casting reaches Safe M + 2 with overreach risk. More PP, Talents and rituals never raise maximum I. I5 itself always requires a ritual.
0: self/touch. 1: within 15 m. 2: within 50 m. 3: any visible point. 4: familiar, marked or mystically linked target in the same realm, ritual. 5: another realm/plane, Mythic ritual.
Range 1-3 needs an unobstructed route. Seeing through a barrier is not enough; Indirect can cross it when the Form permits.
Add each chosen rating once to Magnitude. R marks a ritual-only rating; any rating of 5 also requires a declared lasting mythic price.
Instant, or through the affected subject's next turn.
Until the target next fully rests, maximum 8 hours.
Duration sustains state; never repeats damage, healing or a lost Action.
One; person, door or human-sized object.
Areas include allies unless Selective. Direct Harm uses selected targets, not a radius.
Firebolt at 15 m: Unmake·Fire, I2 + R1 + D0 + Reach0 = M3. Deal 2D6 Projected Harm once; normal armour applies.

Ward two allies at 15 m for a scene: Ward·Earth/Stone, I2 + R1 + D1 + Reach1 = M5. Grant 4 AP against physical blows. At Shaping 60%, the first is safe; the second is Safe + 2: -2P. Ordinary success costs 3 PP or 5 PP respectively.
Use the lowest I that buys the result. Your cell must explain the method; its description never gives free damage, protection or extra actions.
Unmake: I D6. No DM. Choose Projected or Direct delivery before M.
Alter·Flesh: I D4 HP, up to maximum.
2 × I AP against physical, elemental or spiritual harm; both physical and elemental is +1 I. Use it or worn armour, whichever is higher.
2 × I AP; 5 × I total HP. Reach sets footprint.
3 × I points absorb qualifying HP damage after other protection, before HP/MWL.
I2: +1B / -1P. I4: +2B / -2P. Name one skill or narrow family.

Healing also removes Bleeding and Dying. Above 0 HP, act next turn. I3+ counts as Surgery; Wounded ends after treatment when HP exceeds MWL. Like mundane care, only one HP-restoring Shaping helps a subject before its next full rest; stopping Bleeding and Dying alone is never limited. No regeneration pools.

Poison/disease curing needs I × 25 at least Potency, then Shaping must win against Potency. After failure, the same Shaper needs full rest, new treatment, discovery or another meaningful change before retrying.

Keep only the strongest same-kind magical modifier/protection. A reserve cannot refill; keep only the larger of a new reserve or existing remaining points. It changes neither maximum HP nor MWL and absorbs no PP damage or paid sacrifice.
A solid barrier blocks movement and route, never appears through occupied space. Trapping an unwilling subject is hostile restraint: it chooses Dodge or Resilience.
The cell chooses the method. Wings, a force lift and a stone stair can solve the same problem without using the same targets, defences or consequences.
I2: climb/swim or traverse a named surface at normal Movement. I3: fly at normal Movement.
I4: one named mundane substance, half Movement; finish each Movement Action in empty space or return to entry.
I1: +3 m; I2: ×1.5; I3: ×2; I4: ×3. Separate from buying the mode.
I1: Low-Light Sight. I2: Night Vision or narrow environmental sense. I3: Blind Sight with named blocker. I4: broad sense of one defined class.
I1: hold breath 10 minutes. I2: breathe one named medium. I3: no need to breathe.

Use your own Movement Action for a granted mode; the Shaper need not spend an Action maintaining a passive benefit. Dangerous movement can still need Athletics. If flight ends unsupported, you fall. Breathing water gives neither swimming nor protection from pressure, heat or contact hazards.

I1: immediate clue/presence. I2: locate, diagnose, communicate or see through ordinary concealment. I3: distant observation, surface thoughts, deeply hidden evidence. I4: guarded memory, history, motives or possible futures.

Live observation, communication and thought-reading require concentration; static facts and fixed senses do not. Scry cannot reveal evidence absent from accessible minds, places or traces. Senses use Perception when noticing is uncertain. Use only the best relevant sense; blockers and the Form's scope remain.
Price exact consequences. "Paralysed" gives no free damage, helplessness, movement or control.
Prone, or a brief hindrance such as half Movement through next turn.
Restrain; -1P to one skill/family or one sense.
Suppress one sense; remove one Combat Action once; serious tactical compulsion.
No Actions/Reactions while incapacitated; or full bodily/mental control with active maintenance.
A lost Combat Action never repeats; the target is immune until it completes a later Combat Action.

Usually spend a Combat Action to retry the original defence against stored Shaping; win to escape. If Combat Actions are prevented, retry freely at your own turn's end, after its restrictions. Winning does not restore missed Actions; it does not require being conscious.

Example: bind, stored success 42. Resilience 60% rolls 55: success and higher, so you escape. The Shaper does not reroll. Magical sleep can instead end on damage or an adjacent ally's waking Combat Action.

I1 can colour emotion; I2 compels a limited reasonable act, not a combat Action, tactical disadvantage or action against interests. Such compulsion needs I3. Compelled acts use the subject's own turn and Action. An unwilling subject you move by active control goes at most 3 m per round. Full control needs the Shaper's Combat Action; serious self-harm, defining betrayal or violated central belief gives another Persistence defence. Certain death always does.
Dispel active magic. For nonmagical Fatigue, I3 removes Fatigued or reduces Exhausted to Fatigued; I4 removes Exhausted. An ongoing cause remains.
One Combat Action. Keep your Movement and eligible Reactions. You need Practice, Tell, a valid target/route, room in your active limit and PP for full M.

Agree cell, outcomes, M and defence. Roll Shaping. Resolve Counter, then defence; pay PP, then apply the effect. A defence stopping it does not refund the casting cost. A Critical keeps its grade, never maximises magical effect dice.
Up to Safe M: no Magnitude penalty. Safe + 1: -1P. Safe + 2: -2P. Higher M requires a ritual. Removing/cancelling penalties never removes overreach.
Pay half M, rounded up; resolve defence normally.
No effect; lose half M and suffer Backlash.
No intended effect; lose full M and suffer Backlash.
Hero Point rerolls happen before PP loss or Backlash. At 0 PP, the casting resolves first, then living Shapers fall unconscious and concentration ends. PP recovery is on page 8.

First make a no-damage Unarmed Combat delivery attack in that Action; normal Reactions apply. No Talent or off-hand attack. If stopped, spend the Action but no PP and make no Shaping roll. Contact then needs casting and normal resistance. A delivery Critical adds nothing; partial Parry does not stop contact.

The GM resolves Backlash: harm, extra PP loss, a stray effect or Fatigue. I0 is cosmetic only. A calm M0 Trick is free and automatic; under pressure, failure does nothing and Fumble gives an inconvenient Tell, not PP loss or Backlash.
Every defence is an opposed test against the original Shaping result, with no critical demotion. The caster must succeed and win; a winning Active Guard uses Size.
Dodge -1P or Active Guard -1P with a shield, spending a Reaction.

Dodge uses the base Reaction, once per round. Each subject defends separately; same-defence outcomes against one subject share a roll. Ongoing areas store the initial result: leaving suspends the effect; re-entry gives no new defence.

Projected: no extra M; crosses space, normal armour applies. Terrain cover gives caster -1P partial, -2P substantial; complete barriers block the route. Direct: +1 M, selected targets only, never radius. Resilience resists bodily harm; Persistence resists Spirit harm. Ignore nonmagical AP, not Wards or named resistances. No Dodge/guard; Direct still needs a valid route.
Spirit Harm: Direct only, I D6 PP, not HP; Soulless targets are invalid. Mind never deals HP damage. Critical Shaping uses normal effect dice and protection.
Shields: each outcome has an Impact Size

I1 Light · I2 Medium · I3 Heavy · I4 Huge · I5 Beyond Huge. Winning Active Guard: same/larger blocks the outcome; one smaller blocks half its damage, rounded up; two smaller block none. A winning Critical guard blocks all. A separate non-damage outcome needs its own successful Size block. No weapons against magic. Counter: page 59.
Total ongoing Magnitude cannot exceed permanent, unmodified INT. Record each effect's M, Duration and casting result. Dismiss on your turn without an Action.
Passive benefit: needs Duration, no maintenance Action. Examples: armour, subject-directed flight, fixed senses. A Critical still counts full M. An instant effect adds no ongoing M once resolved.

Concentration / active control: your Combat Action each round, only one; keep the subject within Range and a valid route. Damage or serious distraction forces Persistence or maintenance ends. Summon commands instead use 15 m and line of effect. Fixed-duration passive magic normally checks route only when set.

Combat Action + 1 PP; Shaping test for active magic within 15 m. Success gives location/Form; Critical adds Technique, M and state. Failure: nothing; Fumble: false impression and obvious Tell, not Backlash. Veiled magic opposes with its original result. Practice and Tell still apply.

Combat Action; M = target's full M + Range, Reach 0 for one Shaping even if it covers an area. Cast/pay normally. Then you must win an opposed test against a fresh Shaping check rolled for the original caster, using their current unmodified skill, not the stored casting roll. If unknown, use 10 × original M, capped 100%.
Active anchored enchantments can be Dispelled. Completed permanent transformations cannot: reversing them needs a new appropriate Shaping.
These are purchased exceptions. Merely reaching an expertise tier does not grant its similarly named Talent.

Perceive a successful Shaping cast within 15 m, or its projection entering within 15 m. Before defence/effect, spend your base Reaction; you need current PP at least its full M. Oppose Shaping against the original result; you must succeed and win to stop it.
Pay full M either way; a Fumble also causes Backlash at that M. Only one Counter can answer a Shaping, and Counter cannot be Countered.

Counter replaces your own defence. If it fails to stop the Shaping, you cannot then Dodge, guard, or roll Resilience/Persistence against it. Another character's failed Counter leaves your own defence available.

Before ordinary cancellation, ignore one total Penalty die caused by Wounded or grappling on Shaping tests. Both conditions together still remove only one. Other penalties remain; prevented Practice still prevents casting.

Once per round, declare before a Shaping casting roll. After ordinary cancellation, before the cap, remove one remaining Penalty; never gain a Bonus. This does not change M, Safe M, maximum I, ritual requirements or Backlash risk. No benefit to Sense Magic, Dispel or Counter; purchase only once.
If both training Talents apply, use Steady Casting first, then ordinary cancellation, then Shaping Expertise.
Buy the Talent once; its added Magnitude is paid in each build that uses it. Additional distinct outcomes within one known cell need no adjustment Talent.
+1 M: name subjects within an area whom the effect excludes. Without it, an area affects everyone in it, including allies.
+1 M per barrier crossed, where the Form permits. Supplies the route for Range 1-3, concentration/control, or casting past complete cover.

+1 M and -1P to Shaping: conceal the Tell. Noticing it requires Perception opposed by Shaping. Practice stays interruptible; someone detecting the Tell in time can Counter. Without this Talent, a Tell cannot be concealed.
+1 M: combine exactly two known cells, each contributing a distinct permitted outcome. Pay every outcome's I; count shared dials once. One Combat Action, roll, PP payment and Tell.

Each outcome keeps its own delivery, targets, defence and protection. Same-defence outcomes against one subject share a defence roll; different defences/subjects do not. Counter stops the whole Shaping; Dispel ends the whole ongoing Shaping. One outcome can depend on another succeeding, but never earns a discount/refund.
A Trigger stores one already-built effect until a declared observable event. It is not a way to add damage to every hit or choose a target later.
Add +1 M plus a second Duration rating for the wait. The effect still has its own Duration. State the event when building it; hidden qualities require Scry.

An ordinary casting arms it immediately: fix target, cell, outcomes, Range, Reach and all other dials, then check target/route. These choices cannot change when it fires. Counter happens at casting; normal target defence happens when it fires, against the stored Shaping result.

For an Activated/Charged item, activation arms one use and fixes its target and permitted choices. Pay PP or spend the charge then, even if the wait expires. The item's observable event was fixed when made.
One hit can be the event

A successful weapon hit on the already chosen target can trigger magic. Resolve the weapon, then the separate Shaping with its normal defence/protection. It inherits no DM or weapon-Critical benefits. A miss leaves the Trigger waiting.
Damage cannot retaliate for an attack against or harm suffered by the caster, bearer or another protected subject. It cannot repeat on later weapon hits.

"When I next hit that ogre this scene, sear it for 2D6." Unmake·Fire, I2 + R1 + Direct1 + Trigger1 + wait D1 = M6; effect D0, Reach0. The hit fires it once; the ogre still opposes the Direct Harm with Resilience. If the scene ends without the hit, the paid Trigger expires.
These methods can look similar to other magic, but have different targets and limits.
Hide a subject or change a mind

I2: -1P to detect through one sense. I3: imperceptible through one sense. I4: every sense the cell governs. Impairing a perceiver uses the same grades. I3+ sight loss uses Pitch black attack/vision limits; general blindness also quarters Movement, while invisibility does not darken the surroundings.

Conjure·Mind: perceive something absent. Alter·Mind: change/omit what is present. Reach counts each affected mind; each resists Persistence. Later observers, devices and Mindless beings perceive normally. Illusions never harm. A fooled witness can spend an Action to oppose Perception with stored Shaping; winning identifies falsehood, not hidden matter. Failure needs new evidence. Fixed illusions need no maintenance; directing behaviour costs the caster's Action.
Bend·Paths I2: move a willing subject, or unwilling one up to 3 m. I3: unwilling relocation within Range; I4 if relocation alone removes it from the encounter. Unwilling subjects resist Resilience.

Conjure·Paths I3+: stationary one-way portal. Crossing costs a Movement Action and spends its Reach allowance. Range reaches both ends; arrival must be empty, stable, large enough and safe from unavoidable harm/confinement. No free collision, falling, restraint or damage. Invalid arrival moves nobody.

I1: non-numerical omen/coincidence. I2: +1B/-1P; I4: +2B/-2P on a named test or narrow endeavour. Later events require Trigger; hostile Fate faces Persistence. Vows do not compel choice. No HP damage, rerolls, automatic success, chosen dice, extra actions or retroactive changes. Predictions are possibilities.

Conjure creates a temporary being from its Form; calling brings an existing one. Both obey a standing order. You can have only one combat-capable summon or actively controlled subject, whatever the Reach.

Give one short order when casting, such as "guard me" or "hold this door". The summon acts right after you, spending its own Actions and base Reaction on it. Changing the order costs your Movement Action, once per round, within 15 m and line of effect. Out of range, or while you are unconscious, it keeps its last order. It needs Duration, not concentration, and ends at 0 HP, at Duration's end, on dismissal or by Dispel.

Movement 15, PP 0, no DM; it ignores Major Wounds and vanishes at 0 HP. Every conjured being is Soulless, and its Form sets its body, tags, one trait and one drawback. A mind, or removing the drawback, costs +1 I each. Flight, invisibility or spellcasting cost more. Spirit, Paths and Fate conjure none.

Only beings bound to a Form, or linked to you by name, token or blood, answer. Intensity equals its Threat Intensity. An unwilling being resists with Persistence or 20 × Threat Intensity %, whichever is higher. Win and it arrives bound under a standing order; lose and you still pay. On a Fumble, it may arrive free and hostile. Summoned beings cannot summon, give PP or pay ritual prices.
Required for M above Safe + 2; I5; Range 4+; Reach 3+; or Duration 3+. Rituals do not raise maximum I or make powerful effects free.

Spend one hour per M in a prepared place, with full Practice and a fitting focus/offering. Maximum M is the greater of Safe + 2 or twice Safe. Exceeding it needs an exceptional campaign event and a serious lasting price.
Then apply the ritual's +1B, assistance and circumstances, cancel and cap. Failure above Safe is still overreach. Use normal PP payment results.
Share the PP, not the roll

Willing participants stay and join Practice. Pledge full M in a declared order; the leader pledges at least 1 PP and pays the first point. Critical leaves unused pledges unspent. One capable Shaper can Assist; only the leader rolls and suffers Backlash. A Fumble also advances every contributor one Fatigue step; already Exhausted means unconscious 3D6 minutes, waking Fatigued.

Indefinite: leader personally commits full M from current and maximum PP, even on Critical; no contributors. Leave at least 1 available maximum PP unless declared mythic helplessness. Ending restores maximum, not spent current PP.

Any dial at 5 is Mythic: agree a lasting price. Materials are consumed at the start; lasting changes attach after success, or on Fumble only if declared. Permanent mundane creation needs equivalent material. Completed transformations become inactive; supernatural properties remain anchored, Dispellable magic. A price never discounts M, PP, active load or enchantment capacity.
No Shaping skill or cell needed. Items show their maker's Tell; hostile effects face the maker's stored Shaping result.
ANYONE CAN USE AN ENCHANTMENT; ITS COST STILL MATTERS
Active while worn/held; commits your maximum PP equal to M. Removing it restores that maximum.
Combat Action and M PP for each reusable activation. You need enough available PP.
Combat Action and one stored charge; the maker prepaid it. No PP cost to you.

Potions and scrolls are one-charge items, spent on use. A multi-charge item becomes ordinary or is destroyed after its last charge, as its maker declared. Continuous items cannot give a depletable vitality reserve; each new reserve needs an Activated use or stored charge.

Activation fixes its target and allowed choices, paying PP or charge even if the event never occurs. It fires once without another Action. Continuous items cannot use Trigger. No item retaliates with damage or adds Shaping damage to repeated weapon hits; each new effect needs a new paid use.

Sense Magic reveals magic/Form; Critical adds Technique, M and anchored state. Scry the matching Form: I2 diagnoses use and effect; I3 reveals a concealed curse, limitation or Trigger. Do not assume what an unidentified item does.
Destroy its vulnerable anchor or Dispel through it to end the enchantment. Completed permanent transformations are different: they cannot be Dispelled.

Build a Shaping and bind it to a vulnerable physical or spiritual anchor during a ritual. Duration 4 is ordinary enduring work; 5 is Mythic and also needs its lasting price. Your expertise still limits ritual M and outcome I.

Gain Enchantment Capacity equal to permanent, unmodified POW. A bound effect moves its full M into this capacity instead of occupying your PP commitment or active M. It persists without you. Pay the PP for each Charged use when binding it.

Continuous/Activated: count full final M once per effect. Charged: count full M for every unused charge. Each separately bound layer counts. Every effect stays attributed to its original creator, even after sale, gift or theft. Helpers never inherit its capacity cost. Mythic effects have no exemption.

Creation, restoration and increases must fit capacity. Only a permanently ended effect frees capacity: Dispel, destroyed anchor or spent charge. Reusable activation and temporary suppression free none.
If permanent POW loss leaves you over capacity, items persist, but you can create, restore or increase none until the total fits again.

POW 12: one Activated M4 effect uses 4 capacity. Two stored M3 charges use another 6, for 10 total. A third M3 charge would make 13 and cannot fit. Using one M3 charge frees 3 capacity; using the Activated item frees none.
Duration 4 and 5 enchantments commit the maker's full M from maximum PP and active M; a Mythic price is extra.

One-use items (potions, scrolls) skip Duration 4: price the effect with its own Duration, plus 1 for binding; a 1D4 healing potion is M2. Pay its PP when binding; until used it commits like any enchantment, or uses capacity with Enchanter.
